tutorial.card_subtitle: A short tour of every screen
tutorial.every_launch_desc: The tour opens by itself every time you start the app
tutorial.welcome_body: A short tour of the app, one screen at a time. You can leave at any moment with Skip at the top, and come back to it whenever you like from the More tab.
tutorial.home_body: A clock whose face you pick from a gallery of twenty, and under it the next prayer with a live countdown — tap it and it turns over to show the previous prayer and how long ago it was. Below that: your city, where you left off reading, your khatma, the sunnah of the surahs, and the saying of the day.
tutorial.quran_body: A complete text mushaf and five scanned printings. One tap on the page goes full screen; a long press on a verse opens its card — tafsir, translation, i‘rab and word meanings. From the toolbar you jump by surah, page or juz, search in three modes, and pick the page’s theme.
tutorial.recite_body: Continuous recitation that highlights the verse and scrolls the page with it, and repeats a verse as many times as you set. You can change the reciter from the verse card or the toolbar, and download whole surahs to listen offline from the recitations player in More.
tutorial.prayer_body: Times computed for your location by twenty calculation methods, with a manual adjustment for any of them, and the Hijri date. Choose the adhan voice per prayer, set a reminder before it, and keep a standing card in the notification shade for the next prayer. There is also a qibla compass driven by the device’s own sensor.
tutorial.azkar_body: Morning, evening, sleep and other adhkar — each one a card with a counter for its repetitions and its takhrij stated. You can set a daily reminder at a time you choose.
tutorial.tasbeeh_body: Count with a tap on the circle, and pick the phrase and the target — 33, 100, 1000 or no limit. The “longer remembrances” card opens the transmitted adhkar, and the one you pick takes the screen as its own card with its own counter.
tutorial.library_body: Text books to download, read and search; the nine hadith collections with their chapters and each hadith’s takhrij; the hadith encyclopaedia in seven languages; and a set of Islamic channels and websites. One search runs across every book you have downloaded at once.
tutorial.more_body: Here are the recitations player for downloading whole surahs, the ruqyah, the new-Muslim guide, and the Downloads page — where you see everything you have downloaded with its size and remove what you no longer need.
tutorial.themes_body: Four app themes, separate themes for the mushaf page, and fonts and sizes you choose. The interface is in seven languages, and the Quran in forty-five translations you download when you need them.
tutorial.offline_body: The Quran, the adhkar and the prayer times work with no connection. Anything you download — mushaf pages, a recitation, a book, a translation — stays on your device, and you can see its size and delete it from the Downloads page.
tutorial.sources_body: Every piece of content in the app has a source, named with a link you can check yourself, and every hadith grading is attributed to a scholar by name. The full list is in More › Sources.
tutorial.prayer_card_body: Today's times for where you are, and the countdown to the next prayer. Tap the countdown to flip it to the previous one.
tutorial.continue_reading_body: Takes you back to the last verse you stopped at. It appears once you have read something.
tutorial.khatma_body: Start a khatma, set your daily portion, and follow your progress day by day.
tutorial.hadith_card_body: One hadith a day with its takhrij and its grading. The arrows move between them and the star saves one.
tutorial.focus_body: The mushaf alone on screen with the rest of the app closed. Leave it with the button or the back gesture.
tutorial.quote_card_body: A quote from the scholars’ own books, with the book and the page. Swipe or use the arrows to move between them, and tap to open it full screen.

imam_bio.bukhari: Born in Bukhara in 194 AH, died in 256 AH. He travelled in search of hadith to the Hijaz, Syria, Iraq and Egypt, and compiled al-Jami' as-Sahih, for which he required the highest degree of continuity in the chain of transmission.
imam_bio.muslim: Born in Nishapur in 204 AH, died in 261 AH. He studied under al-Bukhari and others, arranged his Sahih by chapter, and gathered all the chains of a single hadith in one place.
imam_bio.abudawud: Born in Sijistan in 202 AH, died in Basra in 275 AH. His Sunan concentrates on the hadiths of legal rulings, and is one of the Six Books.
imam_bio.tirmidhi: Born in Tirmidh in 209 AH, died in 279 AH. His Jami' is distinguished by noting the jurists' differences and their schools after each hadith, and by commenting on its chain.
imam_bio.nasai: Born in Nasa in Khurasan in 215 AH, died in 303 AH. He was known for the precision of his eye for hidden defects in chains and narrators; his Sunan is one of the Six Books.
imam_bio.ibnmajah: Born in Qazwin in 209 AH, died in 273 AH. He arranged his Sunan by chapters of law; it is the sixth of the Six Books.
imam_bio.ahmed: Born in Baghdad in 164 AH, died in 241 AH; the Hanbali school is named after him. He arranged his Musnad by the names of the Companions rather than by chapter.
imam_bio.malik: Born in Madinah in 93 AH and died there in 179 AH; the Maliki school is named after him. Al-Muwatta is among the earliest works compiled, and joins hadith to the practice of the people of Madinah.
imam_bio.darimi: Born in Samarqand in 181 AH, died in 255 AH. He arranged his Sunan by chapters and opened it with an introduction on knowledge, its etiquette, and the merits of the Prophet ﷺ.

guide.pillars_1_b: To bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. These two testimonies are how a person enters Islam, believed in the heart and spoken with the tongue.
guide.pillars_2_b: Five obligatory prayers each day and night: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha, each at its fixed time. Prayer is a direct connection between the servant and their Lord, and is the pillar of Islam — see "Steps of Prayer" in this guide.
guide.pillars_3_b: Giving a set portion (usually 2.5%) of wealth that has reached a minimum threshold (nisab) and been held for a full year, to specific categories of those in need. It purifies wealth and is only obligatory on those who meet the threshold.
guide.pillars_4_b: Abstaining from food, drink, and other invalidators from dawn until sunset throughout the month of Ramadan each Islamic year. Those genuinely unable (illness, travel) have well-defined concessions in Islamic law.
guide.pillars_5_b: A pilgrimage to the Sacred House in Makkah to perform specific rites, once in a lifetime, for anyone physically and financially able to undertake it — not obligatory on those who cannot.
guide.iman_1_b: Belief in Allah's existence, that He alone is the Lord, Sovereign, and Creator of everything, that He alone deserves worship, and that He is described by attributes of perfection, free of any deficiency.
guide.iman_2_b: Belief that Allah created the angels from light, that they are honored servants who never disobey Him, and that they carry out many tasks by His command.
guide.iman_3_b: Belief that Allah revealed scriptures to His messengers — including the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms — with the Quran as the final revelation, superseding what came before it and preserved from alteration.
guide.iman_4_b: Belief that Allah sent messengers to guide humanity, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets, after whom there is no other prophet.
guide.iman_5_b: Belief in resurrection after death, being held to account for one's deeds, and the recompense that follows: Paradise for those who obeyed Allah, the Fire for those who disbelieved and disobeyed.
guide.iman_6_b: Belief that Allah knew, decreed, willed, and created everything — good and bad — before it happened, while affirming that a person still has real choice, for which they are held accountable.
guide.wudu_1_b: Intend in the heart to purify oneself for prayer (the intention is in the heart, not spoken aloud), and say "Bismillah" (in the name of Allah).
guide.wudu_2_b: Wash both hands three times before dipping them into the water.
guide.wudu_3_b: Rinse the mouth and sniff water into the nose then expel it, three times.
guide.wudu_4_b: Wash the face three times, from the hairline to below the chin, and from ear to ear.
guide.wudu_5_h: 5. Washing the Arms to the Elbows
guide.wudu_5_b: Wash the right arm up to and including the elbow three times, then the left arm the same way.
guide.wudu_6_b: Wipe the whole head once with wet hands, from front to back and back to front, then wipe the ears, inside and outside.
guide.wudu_7_h: 7. Washing the Feet to the Ankles
guide.wudu_7_b: Wash the right foot up to and including the ankles three times, running water between the toes, then the left foot the same way.
guide.wudu_8_b: After finishing, say the two testimonies of faith. Whoever says this has all eight gates of Paradise opened for them, to enter from whichever they wish.
guide.prayer_1_b: Perform wudu, face the Qibla, and intend the specific prayer in the heart (silently, not spoken).
guide.prayer_2_b: Raise the hands and say "Allahu Akbar" to enter the prayer, then place the right hand over the left on the chest.
guide.prayer_3_b: Recite Surah Al-Fatiha, then any portion of the Quran, in the first two rak'ahs.
guide.prayer_4_b: Say the takbeer and bow until the back is level, placing the hands on the knees, saying "Subhana rabbiyal 'adheem" (Glory be to my Lord the Great) three times.
guide.prayer_5_b: Say "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) while rising, then "Rabbana wa lakal hamd" (Our Lord, to You is all praise) once fully upright.
guide.prayer_6_b: Say the takbeer and prostrate on seven points (the forehead with the nose, both palms, both knees, the tips of the toes), saying "Subhana rabbiyal a'la" (Glory be to my Lord the Most High) three times.
guide.prayer_7_b: Rise from prostration and sit calmly, saying "Rabbi ghfir li" (My Lord, forgive me), then prostrate a second time the same way.
guide.prayer_8_b: Stand for the next rak'ah and repeat the same sequence, according to how many rak'ahs that prayer has (2 for Fajr, 4 for Dhuhr/Asr/Isha, 3 for Maghrib).
guide.prayer_9_b: Sit after the second rak'ah (and at the end of the prayer) and recite the Tashahhud, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ.
guide.prayer_10_b: End the prayer by turning the head to say the salam to the right, then to the left.
guide.quran_1_b: The Quran is the literal word of Allah, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the angel Gabriel, preserved from any alteration, and its recitation is itself an act of worship.
guide.quran_2_b: It is divided into 114 surahs (chapters) — Meccan (revealed before the migration to Medina) or Medinan (after) — and also into 30 equal parts (juz') to make completing it over a month easier.
guide.quran_3_b: Many new Muslims begin by memorizing Surah Al-Fatiha (recited in every unit of prayer) and the short surahs in the Quran's final section (Juz 'Amma), then progress from there. This app's "Quran" tab has the full text, real recitation, and translated meaning to help with that.

book_desc.adab_al_nafs: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi's work on disciplining and purifying the soul, treating the kinds of soul named in the Qur'an (the one that incites, the tranquil, the self-reproaching), the state of the heart, certainty, and the striving of the wayfarers.
book_desc.al_adab_al_mufrad: Al-Bukhari's book on character and manners, kindness to parents, keeping family ties and good company. He kept it apart from his Sahih and applied a wider condition to it, so not everything in it reaches the grade of al-Jami' as-Sahih.
book_desc.al_aqidah_al_wasitiyyah: Ibn Taymiyyah's celebrated treatise on the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, written at the request of a judge from Wasit, and among the most commented on and widely circulated creedal texts.
book_desc.al_fawaid: One of Ibn al-Qayyim's finest books: scattered benefits, admonitions and wisdoms on creed, conduct and upbringing, arranged not by chapter but by the turns of faith itself.
book_desc.al_hasanah_wa_al_sayyiah: Ibn Taymiyyah's treatise on the causes of good and evil deeds: that ignorance is the root of disobedience, and that beneficial knowledge produces the awe which drives a person to obedience and away from wrong.
book_desc.al_samt_wa_adab_al_lisan: Ibn Abi al-Dunya's work on the merit of silence, guarding the tongue and the harms of speech, gathering hadiths and reports on the manners of speech and silence among the early generations.
book_desc.al_shamail_al_muhammadiyyah: Al-Tirmidhi's collection of what is reported about the Prophet ﷺ in form and character: his appearance, dress, food, worship and manners, arranged by chapter.
book_desc.al_targhib_wal_tarhib: Al-Mundhiri's collection of hadiths encouraging obedience and warning against sin, arranged by chapter. Al-Mundhiri himself points to the grade of many of them; it holds authentic, good and weak reports alike.
book_desc.al_ubudiyyah: Ibn Taymiyyah's treatise on what servitude to Allah alone truly means, and that a servant's perfection lies in the perfection of his servitude to his Lord; among the most important works on the subject.
book_desc.ar_raheeq_al_makhtum: A modern biography of the Prophet ﷺ, awarded first prize in the Muslim World League's competition on the sira, setting the events out year by year with the reports critically sifted.
book_desc.as_seerah_ibn_kathir: The prophetic biography drawn out of al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, in which Ibn Kathir gathered the reports and discussed their chains.
book_desc.as_seerah_nadwi: A biography attentive to the historical setting — the state of the world before the mission and the effect the message had on it — in a fine literary style.
book_desc.bulugh_al_maram: Ibn Hajar gathered the hadiths of legal rulings the jurists relied on, arranged by chapters of law, naming after each hadith who reported it and its grade. One of the best known and most widely studied primers of legal hadith.
book_desc.fiqh_as_seerah_ghazali: A reading of the sira that draws out its lessons, with Shaykh al-Albani's authentication of its hadiths.
book_desc.la_tahzan: A book on the softening of hearts and lightening the burden of the self, gathering verses, reports and wisdoms for facing worry and anxiety.
book_desc.mishkat_al_masabih: An expansion and refinement of al-Baghawi's Masabih al-Sunnah: al-Tibrizi arranged it by chapter, added a third section, and attributed every hadith to the one who reported it. One of the most comprehensive ordered books of the Sunnah.
book_desc.mukhtasar_minhaj_al_qasidin: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi's abridgement of Ibn al-Jawzi's Minhaj al-Qasidin on spiritual purification, character and detachment; one of the central books of conduct among Ahl al-Sunnah.
book_desc.nawadir_al_usul: One of al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi's best known works, explaining principles drawn from prophetic hadith in a distinctive Sufi, formative style. Stated plainly: the book — like its author's standing among the hadith scholars — holds a number of weak and unestablished hadiths alongside the authentic, and should be read with that in mind.
book_desc.nur_al_yaqin: A short, plainly worded biography written for teaching, which became famous and one of the most widely circulated abridgements.
book_desc.qasr_al_amal: Ibn Abi al-Dunya's work on shortening one's hopes and the blame of long hope and procrastination, gathering hadiths and reports from the early generations on preparing for death and hastening to good deeds.
book_desc.rijal_hawl_ar_rasul: Sixty portraits of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a literary style; one of the most widely read introductions to that generation.
book_desc.riyad_as_salihin: The best known digest of hadith on character, manners and the softening of hearts, gathered by Imam al-Nawawi from the two Sahihs and other books of the Sunnah.
book_desc.sahih_al_adab_al_mufrad: The hadiths of al-Adab al-Mufrad that Shaykh Muhammad Nasir al-Din al-Albani graded authentic, set apart from the weak ones.
book_desc.sahih_as_seerah_albani: The parts of Ibn Kathir's sira that al-Albani graded authentic, summarised and annotated by him. He died before completing it, so it ends at 2/94 of Abd al-Wahid's edition.
book_desc.sayd_al_khatir: Ibn al-Jawzi's passing thoughts and reflections on the self, religion and the world; among the most delicate writing on admonition and spiritual formation by the scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah.
book_desc.seerat_ibn_hisham: The earliest biography to reach us complete: Ibn Hisham's refinement of Ibn Ishaq's sira. This electronic copy covers only the first two volumes of the edition named.
book_desc.umdat_al_ahkam: A short primer of the hadiths of legal rulings, in which al-Maqdisi confined himself to what al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported, making it among the most firmly established books of rulings. One of the texts a student begins with.
book_desc.uyun_al_athar: A sira composed on the method of the hadith scholars, covering the expeditions, the Prophet's qualities and his life; one of the standard works of sira among the later scholars.
book_desc.zad_al_maad: The Prophet's ﷺ way in worship, dealings, expeditions and medicine, edited by the two al-Arna'uts. Among the most comprehensive works on prophetic guidance.
book_desc.rawdat_al_uqala: A book of ethics and self-discipline in which Ibn Hibban gathers the sayings of the wise on reason, silence, forbearance and good company.
book_desc.hilyat_al_awliya: A ten-volume encyclopedia of the lives of the ascetics and devout, from the Companions onwards, gathering their accounts and sayings.
book_desc.al_khilaf_asbabuh: A short treatise on why people differ and how to differ well — that disagreement may be a mercy and not a rupture.
book_desc.al_adhkar_nawawi: The classic collection of the remembrances of the day and night and the supplications for every occasion, with their chains and grading.
book_desc.at_tibyan_hamalat_al_quran: The manners of the one who carries the Quran, teaches it and learns it, and the merit and rules of recitation.
book_desc.al_arbaun_an_nawawiyyah: The forty-two hadith al-Nawawi gathered as the pivots of the religion — the most memorised and most commented hadith text there is.
book_desc.bustan_al_arifin: Sittings on detachment, softening the heart and the reports of the knowers, narrated by al-Nawawi with his chains — a small book of great benefit.
book_desc.at_taqrib_wat_taysir: Al-Nawawi’s abridgement in the terminology of hadith, a summary of his own Irshad — a teaching text in the hadith sciences.
book_desc.fadail_al_quran_ibn_kathir: The merit of the Quran, its collection, arrangement, script and its seven readers — the appendix to Ibn Kathir’s tafsir.
book_desc.al_baith_al_hathith: Ibn Kathir’s abridgement of Ibn as-Salah’s introduction to hadith terminology — one of the most studied texts in the field.
book_desc.al_fusul_fi_seerat_ar_rasul: Ibn Kathir’s concise life of the Prophet ﷺ, arranged in chapters.
book_desc.mujizat_an_nabi: The signs of prophethood and the Prophet’s miracles ﷺ, drawn from Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah.
book_desc.musnad_abi_bakr: What Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, gathered with its chains.
book_desc.tuhfat_at_talib: Ibn Kathir’s takhrij of the hadith cited in Ibn al-Hajib’s epitome of legal theory.
book_desc.tabaqat_ash_shafiiyyin: The biographies of the Shafii scholars, generation by generation, from al-Shafii onward.
book_desc.adab_dukhul_al_hammam: A treatise on the manners and rulings of entering the bathhouse and what is reported about it.
book_desc.juz_bay_ummahat_al_awlad: A juristic monograph on the question of selling umm walad, its disagreement and its evidences.
book_desc.madha_khasira_al_alam: Al-Nadwi’s best-known book: a reading of the nations before and after Islam, and what befell the world when the Muslims withdrew from their role.
book_desc.ila_al_islam_min_jadid: A call to return Islam to its place in a Muslim’s life — not as an inheritance but as a choice.
book_desc.al_islam_wal_hukm: A brief treatise on where governance sits within the religion and among the aims of the Sharia.
book_desc.riddah_wala_aba_bakr_laha: An essay on the modern turning away from the religion, and the absence of anyone to stand against it as Abu Bakr once stood.
book_desc.urid_an_atahaddath: A word addressed to those working for Islam, on correcting the intention and straightening the path.
